question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-3y &=-2 \\ 2x+4y &=-14.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -3 & -2 \\ 2 & 4 & -14\end{array}\right].
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -3 & -2 \\ 2 & 4 & -14\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -3 & -2 \\ 0 & 10 & -10\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{10}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -3 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & -1\end{array}\right].\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-3y &=-2 \\ y &=-1,\end{aligned}\right.
$$

and we can apply back substitution. The final equation $y=-1$ tells us the value of $y.$ Substituting this value into the first equation, we get

$$
x-3(-1)=-2\,⇒\,x=-5.
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=-5$ and $y=-1.$
